request: SAML SSO and a SOC 2 Type II report before they sign the expansion.
notes: Procurement was blunt: no SAML SSO and no SOC 2 Type II report, no expansion. Their CISO said they cannot add vendors that need separate logins. Expansion is worth another 300k on top of current ARR.

request: HIPAA deployment inside their own VPC.
notes: They will not send patient-adjacent audio through a shared multi-tenant endpoint. Legal wants a VPC deployment with a BAA. Champion says this is the single blocker for the renewal.

request: Sub-300 ms streaming latency for live station announcements, plus on-prem option.
notes: Renewed for a year but the operations lead warned that announcement latency of 700 ms in peak hours is embarrassing. They also asked whether an on-prem or private cloud install is possible because of data residency rules.

request: Usage analytics dashboard they can share with finance.
notes: Finance keeps asking us for minutes consumed per project and we cannot give it. They are exporting logs and building spreadsheets by hand. Wants a usage dashboard with per-project breakdown and CSV export.

request: Arabic voices, both Modern Standard and Gulf dialect.
notes: They run news bulletins and the current Arabic voices sound like a textbook. Editorial lead said a Gulf dialect voice is the deciding factor for the three-year deal and they have written it into the draft contract.

request: Android SDK with streaming playback parity with iOS.
notes: Renewed on the promise that Android catches up. Their mobile lead has already pushed a feature a quarter and said a second slip means they move voice work to a competitor.

request: Time to first byte under 300 ms and a usage-based pricing tier.
notes: Live dubbing use case. TTFB is around 650 ms today. Also said the fixed seat plan is wrong for them: pay-as-you-go per-minute pricing would let them start immediately.

request: P1 support response within one hour, and webhook retries.
notes: Two outages last quarter, first reply took 9 hours. They want a written support SLA with a 1 hour response on P1 tickets. Also complained webhook deliveries were dropped silently during the incident.

request: Hindi voices and a pronunciation dictionary for names and terminology.
notes: Translation agency needs Hindi urgently, 40 percent of their pipeline. Also wants a custom pronunciation lexicon so product names are read correctly every time.

request: Reliable webhooks with retries and signatures.
notes: Their dispatch system depends on our job-complete webhook. Missed three in a month and nobody noticed until drivers called. Need retries with backoff, signing secrets and a delivery log.

request: SSO plus consent workflow for voice cloning.
notes: Law firm clients need SSO through Okta. Their compliance team also wants documented consent from any person whose voice is cloned, before the clone can be used.

request: Usage analytics API and webhook delivery logs.
notes: Analyst said they would pay more for a usage report API they can pull into their BI tool. Also wants to see which webhooks failed.

request: Unity SDK and a pronunciation dictionary for fantasy character names.
notes: Narrative designers fight the engine every time a character name is mispronounced. Engineers would love a native Unity plugin so they stop wrapping the REST API.

request: Unity or Unreal plugin; voice clone consent flow for actors.
notes: Studio wants an Unreal and Unity plugin. Voice actors are nervous about cloning, so an explicit consent record for each cloned voice would help legally.

request: Pronunciation lexicon for author names and Latin terms.
notes: Editors keep re-recording chapters because names are mispronounced. A shared lexicon across the whole catalog would save them hours each week.

request: Pronunciation dictionary and clone consent paperwork for narrators.
notes: Narrator contracts now require signed consent before a voice clone is created. Also need to correct pronunciation once and have it stick across books.

request: Unreal Engine plugin.
notes: Small studio, Unreal only. They will build around us if there is a plugin, otherwise they use an on-device engine.

request: Usage analytics by campaign, and consent tracking for cloned voices.
notes: Agency bills clients by campaign and has no per-campaign usage report. Brands also ask for proof that talent consented to voice cloning.

request: Usage-based pricing and simple analytics.
notes: Cannot justify the flat plan on a show-by-show basis. A per-minute pay-as-you-go tier plus a usage dashboard would close this next week.

request: Hindi voices and per-minute pricing for a school pilot.
notes: Schools in India want Hindi narration. Budget is tiny and unpredictable, so usage-based billing with overage caps is a must.

request: Better MP3 export; asked about on-prem for the studios.
notes: Mostly happy. Asked for a broadcast-grade MP3 export option and wondered about running an on-prem box inside studios.

request: SSO required by their own customers' security review.
notes: Their customers' security teams ask them for SSO and SOC 2 evidence from every sub-processor, including us.

request: Hindi and usage-based pricing.
notes: Student app, price sensitive. Wants Hindi and a pay-as-you-go option so cost scales with active students.

request: Guaranteed support response time during events.
notes: Ticket drops are time critical. When something breaks on a Friday night they need a response time commitment, not a ticket queue.

request: Android SDK with streaming.
notes: Half their users are on Android. Coaching audio cannot stream on Android so they pre-render everything and users complain about lag.

request: Support SLA and a usage report per property.
notes: Support tickets sit for days. They also need to split usage by property for cost allocation.

request: Lower latency and per-minute pricing.
notes: Voice chat product. Latency is the product. Says anything over 300 ms to first audio breaks conversation flow. Also prefers pay-as-you-go.

request: Swahili voices; maybe Arabic later.
notes: Newsroom in Nairobi. Swahili voice would be a differentiator for them. Mentioned Arabic as a later wish.

request: Webhook reliability and cheaper low-volume pricing.
notes: Order-ready notifications rely on webhooks and some never arrive. They also pay a flat fee for tiny volume and want usage-based pricing.

request: Faster response for phone ordering voice agent.
notes: Callers hang up when the agent pauses. Latency has to come down for phone ordering. Also asked for a Salesforce connector, but that is not a priority.

request: Pronunciation dictionary; a dark mode for the dashboard.
notes: Librarians read author names all day and the tool keeps getting them wrong. Also asked for dark mode, nice to have.

request: Android SDK and cheaper entry pricing.
notes: Hiking audio guides on Android with offline-first streaming. Entry price is too high for a seasonal business, pay-as-you-go would suit.
